source.title: BnMMLU: Measuring Massive Multitask Language Understanding in Bengali

record.file_problem: The full paper is present. Some extracted text and character formatting, especially Bengali script and table typography, is garbled; the model names and English-language results are readable.
record.tranche_reason: It evaluates downstream benchmark accuracy across model sizes and estimated training compute, using a different measure from pretraining-loss scaling studies.
record.gate_note: The paper reports benchmark accuracy by model size and a qualitative accuracy-versus-compute plot, which bear on V6. It does not measure held-out pretraining loss, fit loss power laws, test extrapolation, find compute-optimal parameter/token allocations, or vary architecture at a fixed parameter count. The compute estimate and model sizes are not loss-scaling results. Rows below record the reported BnMMLU-FULL and selected BnMMLU-HARD 0-shot Direct results; other HARD prompt settings and domain-level scores are not separately rowed.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates off-the-shelf model families at several sizes on a new Bengali MCQ benchmark. It reports accuracy against parameter count (Table 8) and against estimated training compute (Figure 8), so its results bear on V6 (downstream improvement with scale) in a new setting. Size series are not controlled sweeps: model generations are mixed within the Llama ladder, and TigerLLM sizes have different bases. It reports no loss, no fits, no allocation and no architecture comparisons, so V1–V5 and V7 are untested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors say scaling generally improves accuracy, with diminishing or sublinear returns and meaningful cross-family differences. They conclude that data and post-training recipe quality matter beyond parameter count. They add that Bengali-centric families appear to plateau earlier than the largest bilingual/global families.
record.recipe_differences: This is a Bengali multiple-choice benchmark evaluation of existing model families, reporting accuracy across sizes and estimated compute rather than controlled pretraining runs measuring held-out cross-entropy loss.
record.method_sensitivity: Accuracy depends on model family and benchmark subset; the authors report gains tapering with compute, cross-family gaps at comparable compute, and non-monotonic scores across some BnMMLU-HARD size series. Prompting and context regime also affect results, but those comparisons are not rows for V6 here.
record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The size comparisons are not controlled same-family training sweeps across all models; several models have undisclosed parameter counts. Compute is estimated from parameters and training tokens, while training-token counts are not reported here. No uncertainty estimates are provided. The compute-accuracy plot is not tabulated with exact point values.
record.rows_left_out: BnMMLU-HARD CoT and 5-shot results (Tables 3 and 9), model/domain breakdowns (Tables 2, 4 and 8), and detailed per-model compute-plot point values (Figure 8) were not separately extracted; this record keeps the aggregate plot description and the 0-shot Direct scores relevant to size-related downstream accuracy.

untested.parts: No pretraining loss measured; no power-law form in N, D or C.
No fits on small runs used to predict larger runs.
No shape or architecture variation at fixed parameter count.
No other modality or training regime examined for power-law form.
No relation to pretraining loss, and no fitted predictive curve or extrapolation; only qualitative monotonicity with size or estimated compute is reported.
No fitted exponents or compute-optimal splits compared across setups.

missing.what: Per-model point values (estimated ExaFLOP and average accuracy) behind the compute-accuracy plot, and the training-token counts used for the 6ND estimate

record.verdict_notes: The study is a benchmark paper, not a scaling study. The scaling evidence comes from heterogeneous off-the-shelf checkpoints: Llama mixes the 3.1, 3.2 and 3.3 generations, and TigerLLM sizes have different bases. Compute is estimated with Kaplan's 6ND formula, but tokens are not tabulated. HARD-subset rows are uninterpretable for scaling because the subset was selected on errors of top models. No uncertainty is reported.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens, or compute; power-law behavior and several-orders-of-magnitude range.
Predicting large-run pretraining loss from power laws fitted on smaller runs.
Loss-minimizing parameter and token allocation at fixed compute, and how either allocation grows with compute.
Architecture comparisons at fixed parameter count.
Scaling-law behavior in other modalities or training regimes such as repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer.

The study evaluates Bengali benchmark accuracy, not pretraining loss; it does not establish a predictive fit or test downstream performance against pretraining loss. Model families are not controlled, matched scaling runs.

It does not fit or compare loss exponents or compute-optimal splits, or test how those fitted quantities depend on counting, schedule, data, or fitting method. Accuracy gains tapering and cross-family differences do not test the loss-law fit claims.

relationships.condition: BnMMLU-FULL 0-shot Direct; Llama 3.x, Qwen3, Gemma 3 and TigerLLM size ladders
relationships.reason: Accuracy rises monotonically with size in each ladder, e.g. Qwen3 36.25→65.34 from 1.7B to 32B and Llama 26.69→61.87 from 1B to 70B (F01–F12, F15–F16).
relationships.display_finding: Accuracy increases monotonically in every size series, including Qwen3 from 36.25 to 65.34 between 1.7B and 32B and Llama from 26.69 to 61.87 between 1B and 70B.

relationships.condition: Bengali-centric TituLLM (1B, 3B) and Bangla Llama (1B–8B) on BnMMLU-FULL 0-shot Direct
relationships.reason: Accuracy stays near 25% chance with no meaningful gain from 1B to 3B or 8B (F13–F14, F17–F19).
relationships.display_finding: Accuracy remained near 25% chance, with no meaningful improvement from 1B to 3B or 8B.

relationships.condition: Accuracy vs estimated training compute across families (Figure 8)
relationships.reason: Authors report gains taper at high compute and cross-family gaps persist at comparable compute, so compute alone does not predict accuracy across families (F25).
relationships.display_finding: Accuracy gains diminished at high compute, and models from different families retained performance gaps at comparable compute.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
